summary: Translating a specification, requirement, or feature request into a structured sequence of implementable tasks.

facts.text: Translating a specification, requirement, or feature request into a structured sequence of implementable tasks.
Break-even point: any change touching 4+ files, any refactor with a coherent end state.
Every plan document must contain these sections in order:
Header - Feature name, one-sentence goal, architecture summary, tech stack
File Map - Table: Action (Create/Modify/Delete) | File path | Responsibility
Tasks - Numbered blocks with checkbox steps, exact code, commands, and expected outputs
Validation - Per-task done criteria + overall acceptance criteria
Not In Scope - Explicit list of excluded work
Delivery: Save to docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-slug>.md unless the user specifies otherwise.

Self-contained documents for autonomous multi-hour execution. Required sections: Purpose, Progress (timestamped checkboxes), Surprises & Discoveries, Decision Log, Context & Orientation, Concrete Steps (exact commands + expected outputs), Validation & Acceptance, Idempotence & Recovery.
Planning Without a Spec - Plan solves the wrong problem
Placeholder Steps - Defers decisions to the implementer
Monolith Tasks - Tasks touching 10+ files are decomposition failures
Plan-Then-Forget - Plan becomes fiction when reality diverges
